features.title: Classes
items: Timetable shows today's classes with the room, your attendance and how long until each one starts. Swipe through the week or open the weekly grid.
Attendance shows each course's percentage, the classes VTOP hasn't posted yet and a calendar with every class marked.

The attendance calculator tells you how many classes you can miss or must attend to reach your goal, counting OD that's still pending. Plan days lets you pick days to skip or attend and shows where each course ends up.
Course pages list each course's classes, files and course plan. Files download straight into your download folder.

features.title: Exams and results
items: Exams lists the date, time, venue and seat of each exam.
Marks shows every assessment of each course and the total.
Grades shows your grade history and CGPA. The planner works out the grades you need for a target CGPA.

features.title: Campus
items: Calendar shows the academic calendar with holidays, exam days and changed working days.
Outing applies for general and weekend outings, cancels them and opens the pass. A request shows as done only after VTOP confirms it.
Biometric shows when you went in and out on any day.

features.title: Tools
items: Docs lists the files in your download folder and the mess menu, with the mess timings you set.
Profile shows your VTOP profile and your mentor.
VTOP opens the full site, already signed in, for pages the app doesn't cover.

features.title: Around the app
items: Everything stays saved on your phone, so pages open without a connection.
The bell next to the round button with your initial lists what changed on VTOP. Background sync checks every few hours and sends a notification when something changes.

items.text: The bell also tells you when an outing is decided, a course gets new files or the academic calendar changes.

items: OTP auto-fill reads VTOP's code from your Gmail with your own Google key, or from a forwarding address.

items.text: Mail forwarding walks you through Gmail in three steps with Gmail's own screens, opens the right Gmail in Chrome and warns you if you confirm it from a Gmail that isn't your college one.
Mail forwarding also lets you reopen Gmail's confirmation from step 2, handles a new confirmation while forwarding is on, and warns in Settings when you had to type an OTP by hand.

items: The home-screen widget shows the next class and today's timetable. Long-press the app icon for Timetable, Attendance and Outing.

items.text: Widgets for attendance (the courses closest to 75% first), the next exam and the mess menu join the timetable widget. All four also work on the lock screen.

items: Live updates put the class that's on now and your outing requests on the lock screen, on Android 16 and later.

items.text: On exam days a live update counts down to your paper with the venue and seat. A class you can't skip shows in red, on Android 17.

items: In class mode turns on Do Not Disturb while a class is on.

items.text: Calendar sync puts your classes for the next two weeks, your exams and the academic calendar's holidays in your phone's calendar. Turn it on in Settings.
A Quick Settings tile turns In class on or off and shows your next class.

items: Assistants that support Android's app functions can read your timetable and attendance, on Android 16 and later.

items.text: Assistants can also read your exams, marks, grades, outings, the academic calendar, today's mess menu and how many classes you can miss.

items: Connection, in Settings, reaches VTOP directly, through a compressing proxy or through the vitapmate server. If the server is down, the app goes straight to VTOP.

items.text: On a weak network, the slow-connection (UDP) mode fetches through the server with far less data.

items: Connected apps pairs the browser extension and makes keys for Claude and other AI apps (MCP).

items.text: When the browser extension or an AI app asks for your VTOP session, opening the app shows who asked: the key's name and the IP it asked from, marked new if the key hasn't used it before. Approve or deny there; a notification follows while your phone signs it in.
Name each key as you like when you make or pair it, and rename it later in Connected apps.

items: Share or print the timetable and grade history as a PDF. Long-press the round button with your initial on either page.

items.text: The app asks before your VTOP cookie leaves the phone and says where it goes, and you can turn the question back on.
Semester Wrapped: after a semester's last class, More shows that semester as a story you can tap through and share as images, with Hide grades for the shared copy.
The app asks before it shares your registration number with the server, and server features (connected apps, OTP forwarding, server routes) wait until you say yes.

Account has your server account: sharing your registration number, linked phones, signing out everywhere and deleting the account. Store on server, in Connected apps, lets connected apps keep working while your phone is off.
Swipe the week strip on the timetable to see next week, or the weeks after.
Pages show verbatim VTOP data by default. Turn on Calculated insights in Settings → Insights (or during setup) for totals, GPAs, projections, cross-page views and calculators.

releases.summary: 3.2.3 rebuilds Semester Wrapped with new slides, a receipt summary and private sharing, fits it to every screen, and shows it whatever your Calculated insights setting.

sections.title: New
items: Semester Wrapped is rebuilt: a day-by-day attendance grid, your attendance through the semester, whether showing up paid off, your GPA across semesters, a semester mixtape, your FFCS verdict, absences VTOP put down to a missing face scan, and a title you unseal.
Guess your attendance before the reveal, flip the summary into a receipt, and share a story or wallpaper with grades, your name or hostel and outings hidden.

sections.title: Improved
items: Semester Wrapped is shorter, with thin slides merged, fits small phones, large screens and bigger text, and shows whatever your Calculated insights setting.

releases.summary: 3.2.2 shows verbatim VTOP data by default with opt-in Calculated insights, makes mail forwarding setup more dependable end to end, surfaces forwarding warnings in Settings, refreshes the About screen, and fixes a hang when restoring an account.

sections.title: New
items: Calculated insights (off by default, in Settings → Insights and during setup): VTOP pages show verbatim VTOP data unless you opt in to derived totals, GPAs, projections, cross-page views and calculators after a timed disclaimer. Classes you can skip now sits under Calculated insights.
Reopen Gmail's confirmation link from step 2 if you left Gmail before tapping Confirm.
New Gmail confirmations that arrive while forwarding is already on now show in the sheet, where you can confirm or dismiss them.
Wrong-Gmail confirmations can be ignored so they no longer hold setup back, and Open college Gmail uses Google's account picker when your college address isn't cached yet.
Settings warns you when you had to type an OTP by hand or when a new Gmail confirmation is waiting.
Redesigned About screen with links moved out of the More footer.

sections.title: Improved
items: Gmail links open in Chrome or your default browser instead of the Gmail app, and step 1 notes to turn on Chrome's Desktop site on a phone.
Copy notes, errors and check feedback now appear inside the mail forwarding sheet instead of behind it, and taps on local actions are never dropped while a check runs.
Returning from Chrome checks for Gmail's confirmation or filter right away, and the Show me guide keeps its header, caption and zoom bounds tidy on smaller screens.

sections.title: Fixed
items: A phone joining an address more than 24 hours after confirmation no longer gets stuck on step 1 waiting for an OTP.
A phone removed from a forwarding address stays removed instead of rejoining on its next check.
Restoring a saved registration number no longer hangs on start, and sharing stays off until your registration number is known.
Toggling registration number sharing, deleting the server account or switching accounts refreshes forwarding right away.
Reconnecting phones show a reconnecting note instead of three ticks and no longer forget the address while waiting to sign in.

releases.summary: 3.2.1 puts the server settings where you use them and shows you which app is asking for your VTOP session, and from where, before you approve it. It also asks before sharing your registration number, seals your saved password with the Android Keystore, and makes OTP sign-in, forwarding and connected apps more dependable.

sections.title: New
items: Setting up mail forwarding is one list of three steps, each with Gmail's own screens under Show me. Gmail opens in Chrome on your college account, Gmail's confirmation is one tap, and the app warns you if you confirm it from a Gmail that isn't your college one. Turning forwarding off shows how to remove it from Gmail too.

The Server page is gone: its settings are where you use them. Account has sharing your registration number, linked phones, signing out everywhere and deleting the server account; Connected apps has session handover and storage; Connection asks before the cookie leaves for server routes.

When a connected app asks for your session, opening the app shows an approve sheet with the key's name and the IP it asked from (new IPs are marked), and a notification follows while your phone signs it in. The extension tells you to open the app instead of waiting for the notification.
Name a key when you make it or pair a browser or AI app, and rename it any time from the key in Connected apps.
Store on server, in Connected apps, lets connected apps keep working while your phone is off. It's your choice, and turning it off deletes what the server holds at once.
Swipe the week strip on the timetable to see next week, or the weeks after.
The app asks before it shares your registration number with the server, and says what it is used for.
Your saved VTOP password is sealed with the Android Keystore. If the Keystore fails, the app keeps the password instead of losing it, and tells you when a locked password signs you out.
Stopping sharing signs the phone out of the server.
OTP auto-fill shows the phones on your forwarding address, and can delete the address everywhere.
Forwarding setup is marked done as soon as Gmail's confirmation arrives.
Connected apps shows a banner while its live connection is failing.
The browser extension signs you in live and follows each step as it happens, with a redesigned popup, a badge on VTOP, and sign-in again after VTOP signs you out.

sections.title: Improved
items: Proving who you are runs in the background and takes less time.
On a weak network, a sign-in to the server that drops halfway no longer makes you prove who you are again.
Pages that need an OTP wait for the code instead of failing.
Saved files and settings are written safely, so a crash or a full phone no longer leaves a half-written page, and old leftovers are cleaned up.
The server keeps you signed in for longer, without proving again.
Sleeping timers share one thread, which saves a little battery.
Every screen uses India's date for today.
Logs leave out secret values.
Reinstalling no longer brings back an old sign-in; sign in again.
Account opens without unlocking; the fingerprint or PIN is asked only to show the saved password.
Each kind of cookie question (server routes, connected apps) can be turned on or off on its own.
When your phone doesn't answer a connected app in time, the app or extension says so and how to fix it, instead of waiting.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Moving keys to this phone no longer signs your other phone out.
A resent OTP shows its own time on the open prompt, and the app looks for mail that arrived after it.
Submitting or resending an OTP on a server sign-in could hang.
An expired OTP is recognised, and when VTOP drops an OTP sign-in the app signs in again by itself.
A wrong saved password no longer asks VTOP again, and signing out while a save was running no longer signs you in again after a restart.
Switching to another student clears the last student's saved things from the app.
A request from a connected app is answered once and expires cleanly.
Connected AI apps like Gemini connect without hitting redirect limits.
Connection reloads each time you open it.
A refresh you cancel no longer leaves pages behind, and a page forgotten while it loads isn't saved.
Docs waits for its list of files instead of showing none, and quick sort picks are saved.
The Google sign-in is kept when Gmail setup is interrupted.
Big numbers in Semester Wrapped shrink to fit beside their heading.
Technical live-update errors stay out of the screen.
A very large session no longer breaks the slow-connection (UDP) mode.
Deleting the server account no longer makes a new one on the next start.

releases.summary: 3.2 moves the app to a new server: live updates, OTP forwarding and server fetches share one connection, and the server checks who you are without your VTOP cookie leaving the phone.

sections.title: New
items: A new server. Live updates, forwarded OTPs and server fetches come over one connection, so they arrive faster and use less battery.
The server checks which student you are with a signed proof from VTOP, so your VTOP cookie no longer has to leave the phone for it.
Exact percentages in the attendance calculator.
A Mess or Exams tab, and picking several files at once in Docs.

sections.title: Improved
items: Sharper PDFs and a smaller app.
OTP forwarding picks up the code faster.

sections.title: Fixed
items: Downloads, links that open the app, the docs viewer and OTP resend.

releases.summary: 3.1 adds Semester Wrapped, calendar sync, new widgets on the home and lock screen, exam live updates and a Quick Settings tile, asks before your VTOP cookie leaves the phone, gives clearer change alerts and loads VTOP pages faster.

sections.title: New
items: Calendar sync, in Settings: your classes for the next two weeks, your exams with venue and seat, and the academic calendar's holidays and exam days go into a Vitap Mate calendar on your phone, so they show in Google Calendar, on your watch and in At a Glance. Turning it off removes that calendar.

New widgets: Attendance lists the courses closest to 75% with how many classes you can miss, Exams counts down to your next paper, and Mess menu shows the meal on now or next. They and the timetable widget also work on the lock screen.
Exam live update: on an exam day, from an hour before, the lock screen counts down to your paper with the venue, seat and reporting time, then to its end.
On Android 17, a class live update turns red when you can't skip it and amber when you can miss only one or two more.
A Quick Settings tile turns In class on or off and shows the class on now or next.

Assistants like Gemini can now read your exams, marks, grades, outing requests, the academic calendar, the mess menu and how many classes you can miss before the next exam, as well as your classes and attendance.

Semester Wrapped: once a semester's classes are over, the top of More opens a story of that semester. Tap through attendance, your longest streak, the courses you never missed, your room and faculty, marks, GPA and CGPA, outings and campus times, then share any slide or the summary card as an image.
Close call: the course that came nearest to 75%, with how many classes you had to spare.
On Duty: how many of your classes were on OD, on how many days, and the course with the most.
Morning or afternoon person, from when your classes started.
Full marks and Assessments: the tests you scored full marks in, and every test you took, by kind. Hide grades leaves full marks out of the shared image.
Exam crunch: your busiest exam week and the most exams in one day.
Hostel life and On the move, from your biometric punches: time out of the hostel, trips back between classes, floors climbed and rooms. These are worked out from punches, so they can be a little off.
Hide grades leaves your marks and grades out of the shared image. The story on your phone still shows them.
Campus times for Wrapped come from VTOP only when you tap Fetch. They load in the background with a notification you can stop.
Before your VTOP cookie goes to the vitapmate server, the app asks first and says where it goes and what it is used for. Tick Don't ask again for each kind, or turn it back on in Settings.
Checking your server account no longer sends your VTOP cookie every time. Once VTOP confirms it, this phone stays confirmed for two weeks.
Connected apps has a button to copy the MCP link, and Make a key by hand for AI apps that take a key instead of signing in.
After the day's last class, the timetable card shows the day as a track of the classes you had.
How strongly the app asks you to update now depends on the release: a small pill, Play's update dialog or a full-screen prompt for important fixes.

sections.title: Improved
items: The timetable widget is rebuilt and follows your wallpaper's colours as before.
In class uses Android 15's Modes, with its own icon and a description of when it turns on.
The forwarding guide and these notes now load when you open them and stay saved on your phone, so they can be corrected without an app update.
OTP auto-fill through a forwarding address matches codes by VTOP's clock and keeps waiting while a code is on its way.
Outing no longer limits the longest trip to 15 days. VTOP decides what it allows.
The source code link in About opens the right GitHub page.
Exams are listed in the order they happen, so a CAT shows before the FAT.
Background sync also saves the last few days of biometric entries.
Silence during classes (Settings → In class) also covers exams, from reporting time until each one ends.
VTOP saves the site's own files on your phone, so pages open faster. Clear saved files is in the VTOP menu.
Pull to refresh in VTOP reopens the page you're on instead of going back to the start. If your session ran out, the app signs in again and reopens it.
With OTP auto-fill on, the app asks VTOP for a new code once if the first one expires before it arrives.
Changes in the bell name the course first and say what happened under it. It also lists outing decisions, new course files and academic calendar changes, and opening a page clears its changes.
Background sync also checks a pending outing, so you hear when it's decided.
Tap a class in Timetable to open that course's attendance.
Course files that Docs can show open in its own viewer.
The app is smaller and starts with less to load.

sections.title: Fixed
items: The app could close by itself right after opening.
The semester sheet and other sheets sometimes ignored every tap.
Signing in with your device lock works on Android 9.
Scanning the QR code in Connected apps uses Google's scanner directly.
The slow-connection (UDP) mode handles a phone clock that's off and retries when needed.
Downloads, links into the app and OTP resend are more reliable.
An error inside the app fails only that action instead of closing the app.

releases.summary: vitapmate 3.0 is a new native Android app. It opens faster, scrolls more smoothly and is a smaller download than the old app. Everything the old app had is still here, and your data is still saved on your phone.

sections.title: New
items: The change inbox, background sync and Fetch all, which refreshes every VTOP page at once.
Change notifications have a channel for each kind, and a Mark as seen button.
Attendance calculator with goals, Plan days and the attendance calendar.
Home-screen widget and launcher shortcuts.
Live updates, In class mode and app functions for assistants.
PDFs of the timetable and grade history.
OTP auto-fill from Gmail or a forwarding address. The app stays awake while you sign in to Google, so it finishes before you come back.
Connection, in Settings, reaches VTOP directly, through a compressing proxy or through the vitapmate server. If the server is down, the app goes straight to VTOP.
Connected apps for the browser extension and AI apps. Each key has its own switch for outings, and AI apps can ask for access and you approve it in the app.
The Server page shows what the server keeps and which phones are linked, and lets you clear or delete it.
Your VTOP password is saved in the phone's password manager, and your sign-in survives a reinstall.
A new app icon in five colours, picked in Settings, and a new splash screen.
Updates from Google Play install inside the app.

sections.title: Improved
items: Timetable cards put the room and attendance on one line, with a countdown under the times. The timetable also marks Lab FAT days and shows the week ahead.
Attendance shows classes VTOP hasn't posted yet and days without classes.
Downloads go through Android's download manager into the folder you pick, under VTOP's file names. Docs lists what's in that folder.
When a refresh fails, your data stays on screen with the reason and a retry button.
Activity, in Settings, lists what the app fetched from VTOP.
